_doc: A finder page (build/finders/README.md). Candidates: tables with one of `tags`; or a `title_words` match in a table whose topics include one of `title_topics` (or has no topics); or a `col_words` match in a table with one of `col_tags` or `col_topics`. `topic_ids` / `tag_ids`: topic and tag pages that get a banner linking to the page; `banner`: its text. `place_notes`: a note shown on a place's page ([[id]] links to another place). `link_groups`: a table whose figures are all for the first place and places within the listed ones links there ("Population across all books"). `place_up`: a place's parent on the page where it differs from the gazetteer. `chart_break`: the year before which a place's chart is squeezed into a strip (default 1850). `top_notes`: a caution shown above the source list on a place's page and on every place within it. `place_merge`: one place's figures (and places within it) shown under another (duplicate gazetteer entries).
name: population
title: Population
blurb: Population figures for every country, colony, prefecture, province, city and district in the tables, year by year, with the contradictions kept and a link to each source table.
title_words: population|inhabitants|人口|戶口|戸口|現住|census|國勢|国勢

banner: Looking for the population of one place in one year? The Population page gathers every figure the tables give for a place, shows where they disagree, and links each figure to its table.

place_notes.kwantung: The leased territory alone. Up to 1936 many tables — the empire censuses and statistical yearbooks above all — print it together with the South Manchuria Railway Zone as one unit (關東州及滿鐵附屬地), often headed just “Kwantung”: those figures are under [[kwantung-zone]], and the zone alone is under [[smr]]. The zone passed to Manchukuo on 1 December 1937, so from 1937 the figures are the territory alone.
place_notes.kwantung-zone: The leased territory and the South Manchuria Railway Zone counted as one unit, as the empire censuses and statistical yearbooks print them up to 1936 (often headed just 關東州 or “Kwantung”). The territory alone is under [[kwantung]], the zone alone under [[smr]]. The zone passed to Manchukuo on 1 December 1937; from 1937 the tables' 關東州 is the territory alone, listed under [[kwantung]].
place_notes.smr: The railway zone alone. Figures for the zone together with the leased territory, as most empire-wide tables print them up to 1936, are under [[kwantung-zone]]; the territory alone is under [[kwantung]]. The zone passed to Manchukuo on 1 December 1937.
place_notes.manchuria: “Manchuria” covers different ground from table to table: before 1932 usually the Three Eastern Provinces (Fengtien or Liaoning, Kirin, Heilungkiang); from 1932 Manchukuo, which added Jehol (taken in 1933) and the Hsingan Mongol provinces; and some tables count the [[kwantung]] and the [[smr]] in while others leave them out (the zone went to Manchukuo in December 1937). Check a table's heading and notes before comparing its figures with another's.
place_notes.empire: What “the Empire” includes varies. In the census tables the 帝國 total is Japan proper, Korea, Taiwan and Karafuto only (76,988,379 in 1920; 97,697,555 in 1935); the [[kwantung-zone]] and the [[nanyo]] are printed below it. A “grand total” adds them back (99,456,818 in 1935), some tables count Kwantung without the Railway Zone, and the yearly series of the statistical yearbooks add Japan proper's 1 October estimate to the colonies' year-end counts. Check what a table's total covers before comparing it with another's.

top_notes.china: The population of the Republic of China before 1949 is notoriously difficult to estimate. Be sure to explore the scholarship around the challenges before making use of any of these statistics.
